Books of Kings.fact: Jehu writes to Samaria, challenging the palace officials to pick Ahab's strongest son, put him on the throne and have him challenge Jehu. They refuse, and so Jehu instead asks for the heads of Ahab's seventy sons.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: After he has had them put inside the city gate of _____, Jehu massacres the remaining members of the House of Ahab in order to fulfil Elijah's prophecy
Books of Kings.fact: After he has had them put inside the city gate of Jezreel, Jehu massacres the remaining members of the House of Ahab in order to fulfil Elijah's prophecy.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: On the way, he meets some of _____'s relatives and has them killed too
Books of Kings.fact: On the way, he meets some of Ahaziah's relatives and has them killed too.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Further along, he meets _____, who becomes his ally
Books of Kings.fact: Further along, he meets Jehonadab, who becomes his ally.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Upon finally reaching _____, he kills the rest of Ahab's family
Books of Kings.fact: Jehu then sets off for Samaria. Upon finally reaching Samaria, he kills the rest of Ahab's family.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Under the guise of preparing a sacrifice for _____, he next summons all the priests of Baal
Books of Kings.fact: Under the guise of preparing a sacrifice for Baal, he next summons all the priests of Baal. He destroys the sacred stone and tears down the temple, replacing it with a toilet, thus ending the worship of Baal.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He destroys the sacred stone and tears down the temple, replacing it with a toilet, thus ending the worship of _____
Books of Kings.fact: Under the guise of preparing a sacrifice for Baal, he next summons all the priests of Baal. He destroys the sacred stone and tears down the temple, replacing it with a toilet, thus ending the worship of Baal.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: However, he does not destroy the golden calves at Bethel and Dan, which was _____'s original sin
Books of Kings.fact: However, he does not destroy the golden calves at Bethel and Dan, which was Jeroboam's original sin.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Nonetheless, God is pleased with his destruction of the Baal religion, and promises that his House will reign in _____ for four generations
Books of Kings.fact: Nonetheless, God is pleased with his destruction of the Baal religion, and promises that his House will reign in Israel for four generations. However, Jehu is not meticulous in his worship of God, so God allows Hazael to conquer large portions of Israel.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: However, Jehu is not meticulous in his worship of God, so God allows _____ to conquer large portions of Israel
Books of Kings.fact: However, Jehu is not meticulous in his worship of God, so God allows Hazael to conquer large portions of Israel.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Jehu dies and is succeeded by his son _____
Books of Kings.fact: Jehu dies and is succeeded by his son Jehoahaz.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He also gives them all the spears and shields from David's day that are kept in the _____
Books of Kings.fact: Seven years later, Jehosheba's husband, the priest Jehoiada, introduces Joash to the army, and informs all five units that they will now be required to guard the Temple on the Sabbath in order to protect Joash. He also gives them all the spears and shields from David's day that are kept in the Temple.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Athaliah claims treason, but _____ has her taken back to the palace and killed
Books of Kings.fact: Seven years later, Jehosheba's husband, the priest Jehoiada, introduces Joash to the army, and informs all five units that they will now be required to guard the Temple on the Sabbath in order to protect Joash. Athaliah claims treason, but Jehoiada has her taken back to the palace and killed.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Next, the altars of _____ are destroyed, thus ending the religion in Judah as well
Books of Kings.fact: Next, the altars of Baal are destroyed, thus ending the religion in Judah as well.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Finally, _____ is taken back to the palace and enthroned
Books of Kings.fact: Joash is crowned and anointed, and proclaimed king by the army. Finally, Joash is taken back to the palace and enthroned.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: When he grows up, his first act is to reform priestly pay, and use whatever is left to repair the _____
Books of Kings.fact: When he grows up, his first act is to reform priestly pay, and use whatever is left to repair the Temple. Twenty-three years later, when the Temple is still not repaired, Joash once again reforms priestly pay so that all money from the Temple treasury goes towards repairs.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: This succeeds, and the _____ is repaired
Books of Kings.fact: When he grows up, his first act is to reform priestly pay, and use whatever is left to repair the Temple. Twenty-three years later, when the Temple is still not repaired, Joash once again reforms priestly pay so that all money from the Temple treasury goes towards repairs.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Hazael is back at war with _____, and it looks like he will cross the border and attack Jerusalem, so Joash sends him gifts and he leaves
Books of Kings.fact: Hazael is back at war with Israel, and it looks like he will cross the border and attack Jerusalem, so Joash sends him gifts and he leaves. Jehoahaz is evil, so God allows Hazael to continue oppressing Israel.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Jehoahaz is evil, so God allows _____ to continue oppressing Israel
Books of Kings.fact: Hazael is back at war with Israel, and it looks like he will cross the border and attack Jerusalem, so Joash sends him gifts and he leaves. Jehoahaz is evil, so God allows Hazael to continue oppressing Israel.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Joash is assassinated and is succeeded by his son _____
Books of Kings.fact: Joash is assassinated and is succeeded by his son Amaziah.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: However, _____ does not get rid of Jeroboam's religion, or remove the Asherah pole in Samaria
Books of Kings.fact: Jehoahaz is evil, so God allows Hazael to continue oppressing Israel. However, Jehoahaz does not get rid of Jeroboam's religion, or remove the Asherah pole in Samaria.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: In addition, the war has almost completely eradicated the _____ army
Books of Kings.fact: In addition, the war has almost completely eradicated the Israelite army.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Jehoahaz dies and is succeeded by his son _____, who continues the evil of the previous kings of Israel
Books of Kings.fact: Jehoahaz dies and is succeeded by his son Jehoash, who continues the evil of the previous kings of Israel.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: The key event of Joash's reign, is the death of _____
Books of Kings.fact: The key event of Joash's reign, is the death of Elisha. Joash throws three, which Elisha is angry about, since it means there will only be three victories there.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Joash throws three, which _____ is angry about, since it means there will only be three victories there
Books of Kings.fact: The key event of Joash's reign, is the death of Elisha. Joash throws three, which Elisha is angry about, since it means there will only be three victories there.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: When Joash goes to see him, he tells him to shoot an arrow out of the east window, and prophesies that, based on this, the _____ will be defeated at Aphek
Books of Kings.fact: When Joash goes to see him, he tells him to shoot an arrow out of the east window, and prophesies that, based on this, the Arameans will be defeated at Aphek.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: During a _____ raid, some Israelite men burying a dead body panic and throw the body in Elisha's tomb
Books of Kings.fact: During a Moabite raid, some Israelite men burying a dead body panic and throw the body in Elisha's tomb.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: As soon as it touches _____'s bones, the dead body returns to life
Books of Kings.fact: Joash throws three, which Elisha is angry about, since it means there will only be three victories there. During a Moabite raid, some Israelite men burying a dead body panic and throw the body in Elisha's tomb.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Hazael dies and is succeeded by his son Ben-_____ III
Books of Kings.fact: Hazael dies and is succeeded by his son Ben-Hadad III.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: As prophesied, _____ defeats him three times, taking back the towns Hazael conquered
Books of Kings.fact: As prophesied, Jehoash defeats him three times, taking back the towns Hazael conquered. Amaziah defeats the Edomites and challenges Israel, but Jehoash advises him to stay at home.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Upon assumption of the throne, he executes his father's assassins, but spares their children in accordance with the _____ law
Books of Kings.fact: Upon assumption of the throne, he executes his father's assassins, but spares their children in accordance with the Mosaic law.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Amaziah defeats the _____ and challenges Israel, but Jehoash advises him to stay at home
Books of Kings.fact: Amaziah defeats the Edomites and challenges Israel, but Jehoash advises him to stay at home.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: The pair meet at _____ and Israel thoroughly defeats Judah, scattering Amaziah's troops and allowing Jehoash to sack Jerusalem
Books of Kings.fact: The pair meet at Beth Shemesh and Israel thoroughly defeats Judah, scattering Amaziah's troops and allowing Jehoash to sack Jerusalem.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Jehoash dies and is succeeded by his son _____ II
Books of Kings.fact: Jehoash dies and is succeeded by his son Jeroboam II.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Amaziah faces a conspiracy and is killed in _____
Books of Kings.fact: Amaziah faces a conspiracy and is killed in Lachish.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He is buried in _____ and succeeded by his son Azariah, who recovers and rebuilds Elath
Books of Kings.fact: The pair meet at Beth Shemesh and Israel thoroughly defeats Judah, scattering Amaziah's troops and allowing Jehoash to sack Jerusalem. He is buried in Jerusalem and succeeded by his son Azariah, who recovers and rebuilds Elath.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He restores _____ territory from Lebo-Hamath to the Dead Sea, in accordance with a prophecy by Jonah
Books of Kings.fact: He restores Israelite territory from Lebo-Hamath to the Dead Sea, in accordance with a prophecy by Jonah. This is because God has promised not to destroy Israel and has seen how much the Israelites are suffering.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: This is because God has promised not to destroy Israel and has seen how much the _____ are suffering
Books of Kings.fact: This is because God has promised not to destroy Israel and has seen how much the Israelites are suffering.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He dies and is succeeded by his son _____
Books of Kings.fact: He dies and is succeeded by his son Zechariah.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He is, however, a leper, and so is relieved of his responsibilities while his son _____ acts as regent
Books of Kings.fact: He is, however, a leper, and so is relieved of his responsibilities while his son Jotham acts as regent. Azariah dies and Jotham succeeds him.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Azariah dies and _____ succeeds him
Books of Kings.fact: He is, however, a leper, and so is relieved of his responsibilities while his son Jotham acts as regent. Azariah dies and Jotham succeeds him.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Zechariah is evil, and falls victim of a conspiracy by _____, who assassinates and succeeds him, thus fulfilling God's promise to Jehu that his family would rule for four generations
Books of Kings.fact: Zechariah is evil, and falls victim of a conspiracy by Shallum, who assassinates and succeeds him, thus fulfilling God's promise to Jehu that his family would rule for four generations. Shallum is himself assassinated and succeeded by Menahem, who attacks Tiphsah, sacks it and rips open its pregnant women.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Shallum is himself assassinated and succeeded by _____, who attacks Tiphsah, sacks it and rips open its pregnant women
Books of Kings.fact: Shallum is himself assassinated and succeeded by Menahem, who attacks Tiphsah, sacks it and rips open its pregnant women. During Menahem's reign, Pul of Assyria (also called Tiglath-Pileser) attacks Israel.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Menahem dies and is succeeded by his son _____, who is assassinated by his official Pekah and fifty mercenaries from Gilead
Books of Kings.fact: Menahem dies and is succeeded by his son Pekahiah, who is assassinated by his official Pekah and fifty mercenaries from Gilead.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Pekah is assassinated by _____, who succeeds him as king
Books of Kings.fact: Pekah is assassinated by Hoshea, who succeeds him as king.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He rebuilds the _____ of the Temple
Books of Kings.fact: He rebuilds the Upper Gate of the Temple.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Aram and _____ attack Judah during his reign
Books of Kings.fact: Aram and Israel attack Judah during his reign.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Rezin, king of _____, retakes Elath and gives it to Edom during the ongoing attacks
Books of Kings.fact: Aram and Israel attack Judah during his reign. Rezin, king of Aram, retakes Elath and gives it to Edom during the ongoing attacks.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: In an attempt to resolve the situation, Ahaz writes to Pul for help, which he gives by capturing _____, deporting its citizens and killing Rezin
Books of Kings.fact: In an attempt to resolve the situation, Ahaz writes to Pul for help, which he gives by capturing Damascus, deporting its citizens and killing Rezin. Ahaz travels to Damascus to meet Pul, and while there sends a sketch of a new altar back to Jerusalem, which is built before he returns.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Ahaz travels to _____ to meet Pul, and while there sends a sketch of a new altar back to Jerusalem, which is built before he returns
Books of Kings.fact: In an attempt to resolve the situation, Ahaz writes to Pul for help, which he gives by capturing Damascus, deporting its citizens and killing Rezin. Ahaz travels to Damascus to meet Pul, and while there sends a sketch of a new altar back to Jerusalem, which is built before he returns.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He places it in the _____ upon his arrival
Books of Kings.fact: He places it in the Temple upon his arrival. To symbolise his deference to the king of Assyria, he then removes much of the decoration in the Temple.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: To symbolise his deference to the king of _____, he then removes much of the decoration in the Temple
Books of Kings.fact: To symbolise his deference to the king of Assyria, he then removes much of the decoration in the Temple. During Hoshea's reign, Shalmaneser of Assyria attacks Israel in response to Israel's maintaining diplomatic relations with Egypt and refusing to pay tribute to Assyria.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Hoshea is evil, but not as bad as the preceding kings of _____
Books of Kings.fact: Hoshea is evil, but not as bad as the preceding kings of Israel. During Hoshea's reign, Shalmaneser of Assyria attacks Israel in response to Israel's maintaining diplomatic relations with Egypt and refusing to pay tribute to Assyria.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: All this happens because _____ has broken the commandments, principally by worshipping other gods and ignoring the prophets
Books of Kings.fact: Hoshea is evil, but not as bad as the preceding kings of Israel. During Hoshea's reign, Shalmaneser of Assyria attacks Israel in response to Israel's maintaining diplomatic relations with Egypt and refusing to pay tribute to Assyria.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Shalmaneser conquers _____ and deports its citizens to Media
Books of Kings.fact: Shalmaneser conquers Samaria and deports its citizens to Media. The king of Assyria then sends his subjects to resettle Samaria, led by an Israelite priest, whose job is to teach them the rites God requires.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: This leaves only Judah, and even they are guilty of following the religious practices introduced by _____
Books of Kings.fact: During Hoshea's reign, Shalmaneser of Assyria attacks Israel in response to Israel's maintaining diplomatic relations with Egypt and refusing to pay tribute to Assyria. All this happens because Israel has broken the commandments, principally by worshipping other gods and ignoring the prophets.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: The king of _____ then sends his subjects to resettle Samaria, led by an Israelite priest, whose job is to teach them the rites God requires
Books of Kings.fact: The king of Assyria then sends his subjects to resettle Samaria, led by an Israelite priest, whose job is to teach them the rites God requires. He breaks his alliance with the Assyrians and defeats the Philistines.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He breaks his alliance with the _____ and defeats the Philistines
Books of Kings.fact: He breaks his alliance with the Assyrians and defeats the Philistines. Following the capture of Samaria, the Assyrians attack Judah, but withdraw in return for money.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Following the capture of _____, the Assyrians attack Judah, but withdraw in return for money
Books of Kings.fact: Following the capture of Samaria, the Assyrians attack Judah, but withdraw in return for money.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: The Assyrians soon attack again, and send a threatening and blasphemous message to _____, supposing that he has sought an alliance with Egypt
Books of Kings.fact: The Assyrians soon attack again, and send a threatening and blasphemous message to Hezekiah, supposing that he has sought an alliance with Egypt. The Assyrian commander then attempts to turn the Judahites against Hezekiah, claiming that he is powerless to protect him, but Hezekiah pre-empts and stops this from happening.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: When Sennacherib, king of _____, hears of the advance of Tirhakah, king of Cush, he retreats, but warns of a coming invasion
Books of Kings.fact: The Assyrians soon attack again, and send a threatening and blasphemous message to Hezekiah, supposing that he has sought an alliance with Egypt. The Assyrian commander then attempts to turn the Judahites against Hezekiah, claiming that he is powerless to protect him, but Hezekiah pre-empts and stops this from happening.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: The Assyrian commander then attempts to turn the _____ against Hezekiah, claiming that he is powerless to protect him, but Hezekiah pre-empts and stops this from happening
Books of Kings.fact: The Assyrian commander then attempts to turn the Judahites against Hezekiah, claiming that he is powerless to protect him, but Hezekiah pre-empts and stops this from happening.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: When Hezekiah hears the message, he sends a delegation to the prophet Isaiah, who tells them that God will save _____ and the kingdom from Assyria
Books of Kings.fact: When Hezekiah hears the message, he sends a delegation to the prophet Isaiah, who tells them that God will save Jerusalem and the kingdom from Assyria.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Hezekiah prays, and _____ sends another prophecy of Assyria's destruction
Books of Kings.fact: When Hezekiah hears the message, he sends a delegation to the prophet Isaiah, who tells them that God will save Jerusalem and the kingdom from Assyria. Hezekiah prays, and Isaiah sends another prophecy of Assyria's destruction.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: God sends an angel to kill the _____, and the remaining Assyrians retreat in horror
Books of Kings.fact: God sends an angel to kill the Assyrians, and the remaining Assyrians retreat in horror.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Hezekiah becomes ill, and _____ tells him he will die
Books of Kings.fact: Hezekiah prays, and Isaiah sends another prophecy of Assyria's destruction. Hezekiah becomes ill, and Isaiah tells him he will die.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Isaiah prescribes a poultice of figs, and _____ recovers
Books of Kings.fact: Hezekiah becomes ill, and Isaiah tells him he will die. Hezekiah prays, and God agrees to give him fifteen more years if he goes to the temple in three days.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: When Hezekiah goes to the _____ and stands on the steps of Ahaz, his shadow moves back ten steps, thus proving God's words to be true
Books of Kings.fact: Hezekiah prays, and God agrees to give him fifteen more years if he goes to the temple in three days. When Hezekiah goes to the Temple and stands on the steps of Ahaz, his shadow moves back ten steps, thus proving God's words to be true.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: The king of _____ sends an embassy to Hezekiah, who shows them everything in the palace
Books of Kings.fact: The king of Babylon sends an embassy to Hezekiah, who shows them everything in the palace. Isaiah prophesies that one day the Babylonians will carry away everything in the palace.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Isaiah prophesies that one day the _____ will carry away everything in the palace
Books of Kings.fact: Isaiah prophesies that one day the Babylonians will carry away everything in the palace.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: However, there is peace for the rest of _____'s reign
Books of Kings.fact: When Hezekiah goes to the Temple and stands on the steps of Ahaz, his shadow moves back ten steps, thus proving God's words to be true. The king of Babylon sends an embassy to Hezekiah, who shows them everything in the palace.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: This breaches the _____-Solomonic covenant, and so God announces that he will destroy Jerusalem because of this apostasy by the king
Books of Kings.fact: This breaches the Davidic-Solomonic covenant, and so God announces that he will destroy Jerusalem because of this apostasy by the king.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: The assassins are executed, and Amon is succeeded by his son _____
Books of Kings.fact: The assassins are executed, and Amon is succeeded by his son Josiah. When Josiah hears the laws which have been broken, he becomes sorrowful and sends a delegation to the prophetess Huldah to ask what to do.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: During this effort, _____, the high priest, finds a copy of the Book of Deuteronomy and has Shaphan, the royal secretary, read it to the king
Books of Kings.fact: During this effort, Hilkiah, the high priest, finds a copy of the Book of Deuteronomy and has Shaphan, the royal secretary, read it to the king.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: When Josiah hears the laws which have been broken, he becomes sorrowful and sends a delegation to the prophetess _____ to ask what to do
Books of Kings.fact: When Josiah hears the laws which have been broken, he becomes sorrowful and sends a delegation to the prophetess Huldah to ask what to do. Huldah tells the delegation that God will destroy Jerusalem, but not until after Josiah has died.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Huldah tells the delegation that God will destroy _____, but not until after Josiah has died
Books of Kings.fact: Huldah tells the delegation that God will destroy Jerusalem, but not until after Josiah has died.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Josiah plans a ceremony to renew the _____ covenant
Books of Kings.fact: Josiah plans a ceremony to renew the Mosaic covenant.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Then, he has _____ remove all the objects dedicated to other gods from the Temple, burn them in the Kidron Valley and take the ashes to Bethel
Books of Kings.fact: Then, he has Hilkiah remove all the objects dedicated to other gods from the Temple, burn them in the Kidron Valley and take the ashes to Bethel.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Finally, he fires the priests of the other gods, desecrates the high places and gets rid of the male shrine prostitutes and weavers of _____ in the temple
Books of Kings.fact: Finally, he fires the priests of the other gods, desecrates the high places and gets rid of the male shrine prostitutes and weavers of Asherah in the temple.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He then instructs his people to celebrate _____, since its celebration had fallen out of use for many years
Books of Kings.fact: He then instructs his people to celebrate Passover, since its celebration had fallen out of use for many years.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He is the best king in the history of _____ and Judah
Books of Kings.fact: He is the best king in the history of Israel and Judah.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Josiah goes to battle against Necho II of Egypt and the king of _____, but is defeated and killed by Necho at Megiddo
Books of Kings.fact: Josiah goes to battle against Necho II of Egypt and the king of Assyria, but is defeated and killed by Necho at Megiddo.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He places another of _____'s sons, Jehoiakim, on the throne, who pays the demands by increasing taxes
Books of Kings.fact: Josiah goes to battle against Necho II of Egypt and the king of Assyria, but is defeated and killed by Necho at Megiddo. He places another of Josiah's sons, Jehoiakim, on the throne, who pays the demands by increasing taxes.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Both of _____'s successors are evil
Books of Kings.fact: Josiah goes to battle against Necho II of Egypt and the king of Assyria, but is defeated and killed by Necho at Megiddo. He places another of Josiah's sons, Jehoiakim, on the throne, who pays the demands by increasing taxes.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Nebuchadnezzar II of _____ invades, and Jehoiakim becomes his vassal for three years until he rebels
Books of Kings.fact: Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon invades, and Jehoiakim becomes his vassal for three years until he rebels. This time, there is no support from Egypt because it has already been invaded by the Babylonians.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: In response to this, in order to fulfil what God had said with regards to _____, a large number of raiders from neighbouring kingdoms and empires attack Judah
Books of Kings.fact: In response to this, in order to fulfil what God had said with regards to Manasseh, a large number of raiders from neighbouring kingdoms and empires attack Judah.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: This time, there is no support from Egypt because it has already been invaded by the _____
Books of Kings.fact: This time, there is no support from Egypt because it has already been invaded by the Babylonians.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Jehoiakim dies and is succeeded by his son _____, who is also evil
Books of Kings.fact: Jehoiakim dies and is succeeded by his son Jehoiachin, who is also evil. Nebuchadnezzar takes Jehoiachin and his family hostage, and takes away everything from the Temple and the palace, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy to Hezekiah.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Nebuchadnezzar takes _____ and his family hostage, and takes away everything from the Temple and the palace, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy to Hezekiah
Books of Kings.fact: Jehoiakim dies and is succeeded by his son Jehoiachin, who is also evil. Nebuchadnezzar takes Jehoiachin and his family hostage, and takes away everything from the Temple and the palace, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy to Hezekiah.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Nebuchadnezzar lays siege to _____, and the Judahites surrender
Books of Kings.fact: Nebuchadnezzar lays siege to Jerusalem, and the Judahites surrender.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He then puts _____'s uncle, Zedekiah, on the throne
Books of Kings.fact: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jehoiachin and his family hostage, and takes away everything from the Temple and the palace, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy to Hezekiah. He then puts Jehoiachin's uncle, Zedekiah, on the throne.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Eventually, he rebels against _____ and Jerusalem is put under siege for two years
Books of Kings.fact: Eventually, he rebels against Nebuchadnezzar and Jerusalem is put under siege for two years. Nebuchadnezzar burns down Jerusalem, including the Temple, the palace and all the important buildings.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: Nebuchadnezzar burns down _____, including the Temple, the palace and all the important buildings
Books of Kings.fact: Eventually, he rebels against Nebuchadnezzar and Jerusalem is put under siege for two years. Nebuchadnezzar burns down Jerusalem, including the Temple, the palace and all the important buildings.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He also kills the remaining priests at _____
Books of Kings.fact: Zedekiah's punishment, which he serves at Riblah, is to watch his sons being killed before having his eyes gouged out and being carried as prisoner to Babylon. He also kills the remaining priests at Riblah.

Books of Kings.subject: International Relations
Books of Kings.question: He appoints _____ as provincial governor
Books of Kings.fact: He appoints Gedaliah as provincial governor.

Brian Molefe.fact: Molefe rose to prominence during his tenure as the CEO of the Public Investment Corporation, heading the secretariat as CEO at the beginning of the corporatisation of the PIC in 2003 through 2010, leaving the organisation with assets under management of R900bn at the expiry of this contract. He is best known for his roles as the CEO of the Public Investment Corporation (2003 –2010), CEO of Transnet (2010 –2015) and Eskom (2015 –2016).

Brian Molefe.subject: International Relations
Brian Molefe.question: In 2015, he was appointed CEO of _____ to address loadshedding
Brian Molefe.fact: In 2015, he was appointed CEO of Eskom to address loadshedding. On resigning, Molefe became further embroiled in controversy when he was illegally awarded a large pension fund payout by the Eskom pension fund.

Brian Molefe.subject: International Relations
Brian Molefe.question: Between 1997 and 2003 he assumed a number of senior positions within the _____ most notably as a DDG (Deputy Director-General), including work on intergovernmental relations and asset management
Brian Molefe.fact: Between 1997 and 2003 he assumed a number of senior positions within the National Treasury most notably as a DDG (Deputy Director-General), including work on intergovernmental relations and asset management. He has also held the position of Deputy Director General in the National Treasury responsible for Assets and Liabilities Management.

Brian Molefe.subject: International Relations
Brian Molefe.question: He oversaw a fundamental restructuring of _____'s domestic and foreign debt portfolio between 2000 and 2003
Brian Molefe.fact: He introduced shareholder activism at the PIC and advocated for the transformation of the South African Corporate sector to be more inclusive and representative of indigenous South Africans who had suffered under the policy of apartheid. He oversaw a fundamental restructuring of South Africa's domestic and foreign debt portfolio between 2000 and 2003.

Brian Molefe.subject: International Relations
Brian Molefe.question: The Gauteng North High Court ordered Molefe to repay an amount of R10._____, which he was not entitled to as per a retirement agreement
Brian Molefe.fact: The Gauteng North High Court ordered Molefe to repay an amount of R10.3m, which he was not entitled to as per a retirement agreement. The Eskom Pension Fund launched a court application in which it sought to have the R10.3m judgment enforced.

Brian Molefe.question: In January 2017 Molefe was sworn in as a member of _____, but he resigned, effective, by 14 May 2017
Brian Molefe.fact: In January 2017 Molefe was sworn in as a member of Parliament, but he resigned, effective, by 14 May 2017.

Brian Molefe.subject: International Relations
Brian Molefe.question: In 2017 Molefe was briefly and controversially appointed as a Colonel in the _____
Brian Molefe.fact: In 2017 Molefe was briefly and controversially appointed as a Colonel in the South African Army Reserves.

Brian Molefe.subject: International Relations
Brian Molefe.question: The fourth part of the _____ report, released on 29 April 2022, recommended that Molefe be criminally prosecuted for his alleged involvement in corruption
Brian Molefe.fact: In Part 2 Volume 1 of the Zondo Commission Report, Molefe is identified as one of the “primary architects and implementers of State Capture at Transnet” during his tenure as CEO of Transnet. The fourth part of the Zondo Commission report, released on 29 April 2022, recommended that Molefe be criminally prosecuted for his alleged involvement in corruption.
